decisions.reason: Separate LED and sensor power control does not change the daughterboard's specified LED count, addressable type, or board form.
The source does not specify any connector, pinout, power-chain, or interboard-signal change; the existing 5V_EN signal can remain valid without propagation.

This Requirement already identifies the switchable 5V boost rail as powering the SPS30 and ZE08 sensors, with LEDs absent from its current powered-load list, so separate LED control requires no state change.
Separating load control does not necessarily change which voltage rails are monitored, the monitor device, or the stated 3.3V measurement coverage.
The source concerns LED-versus-sensor control and does not alter DCDC1 voltage, rating, or its normal-operation role on the 3.3V rail.
The separate control of LED and sensor power does not change the standalone USB 3.3V regulator, activation condition, source selection, or powered 3.3V rail.
The source does not change how charge status is displayed or the dedicated CHGLED connector and resistor interface.
Separate LED and sensor power control does not entail a change to the sensor board's connector count, module fanout, or documented connector pinouts.
The SPS30 remains a 5V I2C sensor, and the source does not change its connector, supply voltage, bus signals, or SEL connection.
Separate downstream control does not change the AXP2101 as the normal-operation power source or its battery input range and overall source coverage.
The source does not affect USB data lines, enumeration, flashing, or the USB-C programming-port role.
The message establishes separate control conceptually but provides no new GPIO assignment and does not replace any existing GPIO mapping.
